statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the unique stable array reachable from nums by zero or more legal replacements. Equivalently: (1) r is reachable from nums by zero or more legal replacements; (2) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, gcd(r[i], r[i+1]) = 1; and (3) for every array s of i64 values that is reachable from nums by zero or more legal replacements and satisfies gcd(s[i], s[i+1]) = 1 for every 0 <= i < len(s)-1, we have len(s) = len(r) and s[i] = r[i] for every 0 <= i < len(r).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n, and the problem's final-value guarantee holds: every stable array reachable from nums by legal replacements has all entries at most 100000000. A legal replacement replaces adjacent entries x,y with gcd(x,y) > 1 by their least common multiple; an array is stable if no adjacent pair has gcd greater than 1.
